detach140.report:
# Detach140: complete retail map and bounded probes

Row `dungeon/func_8009DB44`, runtime `func_800A32A4`: 134 words.
The recorded stock recipe is `2.7.2-cdk-G0`. The frozen baseline is exact.
The complete `retail.dis` was read before candidate compilation.

## Retail map

The frame is 32 bytes; s0 holds the record, s1 the update mode and s2 the entry.
Words 0–22 remove three effect types, test record flag 29 and call the detach
helper. Words 23–37 prepare and scan four slots: v1 is the index, a2 the global
page, a3 the flag mask, t2 the registry, t1 the snapshot array and t0 the copy
limit at record + 128. Words 38–58 clear flags and ownership, load the entry,
clear bit 5, and reload the world pointer before clearing its slot at offset D0.

Words 59–71 extract the entry's low five bits, compute index * 140, publish the
destination in the registry and place source/destination in a3/a2. Words 72–82
copy eight 16-byte blocks with v0/v1/a0/a1 as scratch. Words 83–89 copy the final
12 bytes, with the last store in the jump delay slot. Final copy cursors are
dead. Words 90–92 close the scan, 93–117 update counters/mode, 118–126 conditionally
call the update helper and return the entry, and 127–133 restore the frame.

## Prediction and result

The existing `S_800E3E48` is 140 bytes with alignment four. A whole assignment
should reproduce the block and tail operations. The isolated volatile tail is
not supported by the surrounding ordinary RAM declarations; this diagnostic
removes it, but any future landing still needs a completed source-access review.
No candidate here was promoted.

| Candidate | Pins | Words | Distance |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Frozen source | 2 | 134 | 0 |
| Whole aggregate, bindings retained | 2 | 133 | 6 |
| Whole aggregate, bindings erased | 0 | 132 | 11 |
| Whole aggregate, ordinary do/while scan | 0 | 135 | 21 |

The zero-pin aggregate reproduces the entire copy and tail. Its residual is
outside the transfer: the flag mask and copy limit move inside the slot scan,
mode/source moves reorder, and a commutative address add reverses its operands.
The natural do/while scan hoists the mask and limit as predicted, but also hoists
two record-flag constants that retail leaves inside, changing allocation.

The next question is the original scan and world-object model, particularly why
those invariants have different loop membership. Recover the real slot arrays
or an independently exact sibling before another source probe. Do not invent
`end - 128` uses or dependencies merely to keep the limit alive. This is a bounded
negative for three specific candidates, not an impossibility claim.

copy48_transfer.report:
# Round 44 bounded copy result

The nine-row named inventory found no remaining untested alignment-2,
two-path table copy. This statement is limited to the supplied cohort; it is
not a claim about all DUNGEON sources.

One grounded transfer was tested: `dungeon/func_80D137FC`. Its retail
48-byte mover has the same source, destination, scratch-register, loop, and
delay-slot fingerprint as the exact Round 43 aggregate family. The frozen
baseline is exact at recorded `2.7.2-cdk-G0`, 404/404 words.

The first probe replaced the manual loop with a real 48-byte aggregate,
restored the real two-argument registration call, and removed the sole pin. It
kept the retail copy-loop shape but rotated the three saved argument roles
throughout the function, scoring 51 (43 substitutions, 8 indels).

The second and final probe kept the unrelated `action` pin while applying the
same transfer and helper correction. It is byte-exact, 404/404 words with zero
substitutions and indels, but still contains one pin and therefore provides no
pin-removal gain. No broader source search or allocator grind was started.

This checkpoint is a bounded negative for production repair. No output was
prepared for application, and no source, configuration, ledger, or build-root
file was changed.

The kept base is synthesized from literal page 0x800E0000 and typed s8*, while the record index uses a 20-byte stride.
This is multi-axis byte-pointer coordinate arithmetic with keeps on computed endpoints and indices, not one kept typed table lookup.
The four-byte lookup converts D_8017610C to an s32 base; local keeps are on effect and dependent values, not the table base.
The kept void** is dereferenced directly; the later depth-times-four offset indexes an opaque byte-addressed render state and is not table[index].
The relevant indexed points live in a local frame, and the kept bases also mix literal/global page construction.
The four-byte direction lookup is into local direction_steps storage; other table keeps construct literal 0x80020000 pages.
The object-index-times-four expression overlays a large synthetic struct at sequence+offset; the base is not locally kept and the array layout is unproven.
The s16 lookup has a matching two-byte scale but its kept base is repeatedly built from literal page 0x80070000.
